Scan a book\'s barcode and it finds the book\'s call number, then lists the whole collection in shelf order.

To look a book up, Shelf sends its ISBN or LCCN, or the title and author you search for, to the Library of Congress catalog (lx2.loc.gov) and to Open Library (openlibrary.org). The Library of Congress answers only over plain HTTP, so what goes to it is not encrypted. When they have no Dewey number for a book, its ISBN also goes to that country\'s national library: Norway\'s (api.nb.no) for an ISBN starting 978-82, Germany\'s (services.dnb.de) for 978-3, Sweden\'s LIBRIS (libris.kb.se) for 978-91, Finland\'s Finna (api.finna.fi) for 978-951 and 978-952, the Netherlands\' (jsru.kb.nl) for 978-90 and 978-94, France\'s (catalogue.bnf.fr) for 978-2 and 979-10, Poland\'s (data.bn.org.pl) for 978-83, Portugal\'s PORBASE (urn.porbase.org) for 978-972 and 978-989. An ISBN none of these knows goes to K10plus, the German libraries\' union catalog (sru.k10plus.de), and then to Google Books (www.googleapis.com). Nothing else about you or your books goes with it, and none needs an account.

If you sign in to Nextcloud, the catalog and a spreadsheet of the shelf order sync with the folder you choose on that server, and with every phone signed in to it; while Shelf is open it checks that folder every 15 seconds for books another phone added. Your sign-in details are kept on this phone. Nothing is sent to the app\'s maker.

The camera reads barcodes, printed ISBNs and Nextcloud\'s sign-in code on the phone; no picture is kept or sent. If Audio Reader is installed, a book\'s page asks it, on the phone, whether it has that book. There are no ads, no analytics and no tracking. Spreadsheets you save go only where you choose to save them.
This app is free software under the GNU General Public License v3. It comes with no warranty: use it at your own risk. Call numbers come from the catalogs and can be wrong.

Built with Mudita MMD, AndroidX, Jetpack Compose, CameraX, OkHttp and Kotlin; barcodes are read with zxing-cpp and printed numbers with Tesseract (with Leptonica, libjpeg and libpng) and its English model; the Lato typeface and Material Symbols icons. This app is made by wander wildwood, an independent developer: one person, not a company. That makes wander wildwood the data controller for anything the app itself handles, and that is very little: what you put in stays on this phone. The only things that go out are the lookups described above, a book\'s ISBN or LCCN, or the title and author you search for, sent to the Library of Congress and Open Library, an ISBN to the national libraries and Google Books as above, and, only if you sign in, the catalog written to your own Nextcloud server. The developer receives nothing.
Write to email@wanderthe.dev, about your data or anything else.

Under the GDPR you can ask to see the data held about you, to have it corrected or deleted, to limit or object to its use, to take a copy with you, to withdraw consent, and to complain to a data protection authority. Since the app keeps what it stores only on your phone, you can do most of this yourself: edit or delete a book in the app, save the catalog as a spreadsheet, clear the app\'s data in Android\'s settings, or uninstall the app. What the Library of Congress, Open Library, the national libraries and Google Books receive is covered by their own privacy policies. A server of your own is yours: what it keeps is up to you.
